target: Route "b3-level": the third blow-up level — realise B^3 (7-cube, height 22) and measure the cost of one level

findings.result_name: b3:free-parity (clause (a)), and the route's headline "thm:blowup is relaxed"
findings.defect: Clause (a) — B_{p,z}(s) is an AUSO with sink (0,0,o xor z) for EVERY parity function p and EVERY translation z — is already in the repository, twice, and is uncited. The route gives a hand proof and 2600 random samples as its "verification" of a statement the project has already machine-checked in Lean 4. This is an unlabelled rediscovery of the project's own result, and it is the route's headline.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.6311 lem:blowup-faces: "let z be any translation vector and B=B(s,z) the outmap defined as in Cref{thm:blowup} but with inner part s(v oplus z) on the layer (0,0) --- the theorem's unique-sink and acyclicity arguments use only that v -> s(v oplus z) is an acyclic unique sink orientation, so B(s,z) is one for every z, which is the generality the Lean formalisation proves" (l.6315-6318) — the route's proof of (a) is the same argument in the same words. frontier.tex l.5368-5372 rem:blowup-measured: the Lean file "proves ... isUSO_blow (for every z and every parity function), isAcyclic_blow (likewise)". /data/ssg-proof/lean/SSGProof/Blowup.lean l.103 defines `blow (s) (z : V iota) (par : V iota -> Bool)` with inner part `s (xorV v z)` on layer (0,0) and outer part `outA a b (par v)`, `outB a b (par v)`; l.207 `theorem isUSO_blow (s) (hs : IsUSO s) (z) (par) : IsUSO (blow s z par)`; l.313 `theorem isAcyclic_blow (s) (hs : IsAcyclic s) (z) (par)`. The z-freedom among maximal-height translates that the headline advertises as new ("x 4") is likewise already in rem:blowup-measured ("the other vertices of maximal height, of which there are several at every level, give other translation vectors") and cor:blowup-transl l.6356 ("the other vertices of maximal height give translation vectors of weight 2 and 3"). What IS new is only clause (b): the decoupled height h(u)+2+h(o xor z) and "p need agree with h mod 2 only along the walk" — and (b) is an immediate reading of the existing Lean proof, whose `phase_one` evaluates `par` only at walk vertices and whose `phase_two` walks layer (0,0) in the coordinates y = v xor z. So the advertised "2^23-fold relaxation" is really 2^21 (the p-freedom), and it relaxes only the half the route then realises, not the translated layer.

findings.defect: The proof is invalid: it asserts that a coordinate of a unique sink orientation of dimension >= 2 cannot be constant. That is false — the uniform ("combed") USO s(v) = {i : v_i = 0} of the d-cube is an acyclic USO in which EVERY coordinate is constant. The lemma is therefore unproved as stated and false in the generality claimed; it needs the hypothesis "g_j is non-constant in s". The route states (c) as proved and the abstract lists b3:rise-sign as "proved".
findings.evidence: Route LaTeX, proof of b3:rise-sign(c): "If w>=0 then w.(y_v-x_v)>=0 for all v by (a), so Delta_j(y_v)>0 for all v and g_j is constant on the inner cube, which no coordinate of a unique sink orientation of dimension >=2 has." Counterexample: the 2-cube s(00)={a,b}, s(10)={b}, s(01)={a}, s(11)=empty satisfies Szabo-Welzl on all six pairs and is acyclic, with g_a = g_b = + everywhere. The intended application is unaffected: I verified {g^{B^2}_{alpha_2} = +} = {17,19,23,25,27,31}, non-constant (audit-b3, integer arithmetic). At the level-one case, where the seed's g_j IS constant (a 1-cube), the conclusion nonetheless holds — I computed w for the three Max vertices of B1_game.json exactly and the translated coordinate has w = (13/64, -35/64, -5/16), both signs — so the conclusion may well be true; the given proof does not establish it.

findings.defect: The mechanism is prop:rows-turn / cor:b2-rows, uncited. "w has entries of both signs for the translated coordinate" is the immediate specialisation of prop:rows-turn to B_{p,e_j}(s), where g_j is + on layer (0,0) and - elsewhere and so is neither up- nor down-closed. Clause (a) is lem:switch (correctly cited); clause (b) is one line from the blow-up's own definition.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.5449 prop:rows-turn: "If hat p^{i,1} >= hat p^{i,0} then {g_i=+} is up-closed for preceq, and down-closed if hat p^{i,1} <= hat p^{i,0}; so if {g_i=+} is neither, the two reduced rows of x_i are incomparable." l.5465 cor:b2-rows applies exactly this to every Max vertex of a B^2 realisation. The route's LaTeX for b3:rise-sign cites only lem:switch and b3:translate. (The route's w is the unreduced row difference and prop:rows-turn's is the reduced one, so the two are not literally identical statements — but the argument is the same and the route's is the weaker conclusion.)

findings.result_name: The route's stated gap ("equivalently (b3:decompose), there is a nondegenerate stopping SSG with seven Max vertices whose improvement outmap is B_{p,e_{alpha_2}}(B^2)")
findings.defect: The word "equivalently" is false. b3:decompose is a SUFFICIENT reduction under four structural hypotheses the route imposes (action 0 of alpha reads only beta; action 0 of beta reads only alpha; action 1 of beta does not read alpha; no vertex of I u Y reads alpha). The row-family statement implies the SSG statement; the converse needs every realisation to have that shape, which is nowhere proved. Stating the gap inside the route's own design shape makes it look narrower — hence closer to closure — than it is.
findings.evidence: Route JSON "gap" field. b3:decompose's own statement is conditional ("Let G be a stopping SSG with Vmax = I u {alpha,beta} ... whose rows satisfy: ..."); its proof establishes only that such a G decomposes. I confirmed the four hypotheses do hold for prop:b2-realised (checked row by row against B2_small_nf.json: alpha_2's rows are [0,0,0,0,502,0]+8/512 and [71,293,23,0,0,0]; beta_2's are [0,0,0,509,0,0] and [0,0,0,0,0,419]+1/512; no inner or Min row has a nonzero alpha_2 entry) — so the reduction is a faithful abstraction of the only known level transition, which is a point in its favour, but sufficiency is not equivalence.

findings.result_name: b3:tb, and the route's verdict "strict-progress" on the pivot
findings.defect: The construction realises exactly the two ingredients rem:blowup-realise already records as AVAILABLE, and does not touch the ingredient it names as the obstacle. b3:tb takes z = 0: the level-two normal form is reused literally unchanged, the six inner vertices read neither alpha_3 nor beta_3, so the coupling is one-way and the inner values are identical in all four layers. Its height 12 is exactly h*(5) + h*(2), i.e. lem:hstar-super's additive bound — the linear-growth regime the paper has already classified as settling nothing.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex rem:blowup-realise l.5656: "Two of its three ingredients are available. Its outer coordinates switch in every round of the inner walk, and a switching vertex of a game can do that: on the ladder L_n a Max vertex ... flips up to 3,4,4,4,7,8,8,8 times ... And the inner walk is run twice ... The third ingredient needs care ... The obstacle is the operation. On that layer every inner vertex must compare its options as it would at v oplus e_j ... the inner game would have to be shown the anti-value ..."; and "The substitutes we did try ... give heights 4,10,16,23,30, at most 4,6,8 and at most 4,8,10 respectively ... that is linear growth." I verified row-by-row that TB_nf_D10.json's rows 0-4 and 7 are B2_small_nf.json's twelve rows with denominators doubled (e.g. 3/128 = 12/512, 69/128 = 276/512, 115/128 = 460/512, 59/64 = 472/512, all twelve match), and that only rows 5 and 6 (alpha_3, beta_3) are new and that no inner row has a nonzero entry in slots 5 or 6. lem:hstar-super (l.5119) gives h*(7) >= h*(5) + h*(2) = 12.

findings.result_name: b3:cost ("the outer half is now known to be additive (+2 Max, +0 Min, +1 bit)")
findings.defect: Two defects. (i) The two halves are not independent, so the datum does not measure the outer half of a REAL level: the outer readout Psi_alpha, Psi_beta reads the layer-(0,0) inner values, and the translation is precisely a change of those values (b3:theta-floor says so itself); with a translated inner system the outer rows must be redesigned and their cost is unmeasured. (ii) The vertex-count column is not a well-defined cost — the paper realises B^1 on 39 vertices, not 58, so "+80" for B^1 -> B^2 is an artefact of which search found which game. The row that matters (Max, Min, bits) rests on one measured step for the outer half and one published step for the full level.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex prop:m3-realised l.6675: "the first blow-up level B(1-cube)=(0,1,3,6,7,4,5,2) of Cref{rem:blowup-measured} is realised on 39 vertices rather than 58." The route's table uses 58 with a parenthetical. b3:theta-floor's own conclusion — "in a level-three realisation built on those rows the inner vertices must read the new outer pair (alpha_3,beta_3) hard enough to lift the readout of alpha_2 by at least 0.065 on the layer (0,0) and by nothing at all on the other three" — is exactly the statement that the outer design of b3:tb does not survive the translation.

findings.defect: Duplicates existing material and is standard USO relabelling presented without attribution. The m = 2 case is stated verbatim in rem:blowup-measured; the 2-face case is the content of cor:blowup-transl's proof; and translation of a USO is textbook (Szabo-Welzl / Schurr-Szabo, from memory, unchecked).
findings.evidence: frontier.tex rem:blowup-measured: "On its layer (0,0) the inner 2-cube is translated by a single coordinate j: the vertex j has its preference reversed and the other inner vertex compares its options as it would if j were flipped --- exactly the operation that Cref{rem:blowup-realise} identifies as the obstacle." cor:blowup-transl l.6356 proof: "For z=e_i and a 2-face F on {i,j}, G is F translated by the local coordinate i, so the source--sink pair of G is that of F translated by e_i ...". Neither is cited by b3:translate.

findings.defect: Its hypothesis excludes exactly the case at issue, so as a constraint on the open question it is close to vacuous. The lemma assumes "the inner vertices do not read the outer pair, so that the inner values z_v are fixed" — a one-way coupling, which by b3:decompose's own analysis cannot produce a translated layer. It constrains only the family of designs that cannot double. Its real use is as a design certificate for b3:tb, which is legitimate but is not what the statement claims.
findings.evidence: Route LaTeX b3:two-cycle: "suppose the inner vertices do not read the outer pair, so that the inner values z_v are fixed." The level-two realisation, which does achieve a translation, violates this: its inner rows read beta_2 (verified — e.g. x's action 1 is [276,0,0,0,127,0], beta_1's action 1 is [267,187,0,0,56,0]). Its numerics, however, are exact and I reproduced them: the tightest dominance pair is (20,28) forcing 1-AA' < 78974227846783/2781927489443544 = 0.0283883, (16,8) forcing < 0.0311841, against 3313/131072 = 0.0252762 for prop:b2-realised and 4093/1048576 = 0.0039034 for b3:tb.

findings.defect: The headline consequence is conditional on a design choice, not on the problem. The general clause (a closed two-cycle pins val(j) = Theta = q/(1-AA') absolutely, whatever the rest) is correct and clean; the punchline ("a level-three realisation on those rows must lift the readout of alpha_2 by at least 0.065") holds only for realisations that REUSE the published level-two outer rows. The route concedes this in next_steps(2) but the proposition reads more strongly.
findings.evidence: I confirmed the numbers exactly: on prop:b2-realised, val(alpha_2) = 2048/3313 and val(beta_2) = 2036/3313 at all eight layer-(0,0) strategies, independently of the inner strategy; 1-AA' = 3313/131072; the layer-(0,0) inner values lie in [174119728/379997415, 29188096000/52702783249] = [0.4582, 0.5538] and elsewhere in [0, 0.4635]; val(beta_2) elsewhere is at most 0.3476. Theta = 0.618171 > 0.5538.

findings.defect: Three of the four things reported are already in the paper. Height 22 at level three is in rem:blowup-measured; the count of 28 forbidden pairs is in cor:b2-min; non-Holt-Klee for B(B^2,z) at every z and every u is in cor:blowup-transl. New: the explicit 7-cube outmap in print, the walk, "18 distinct 2-faces", and the 16 forbidden pairs of the p-modified target.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex rem:blowup-measured: "the heights are 4,10,22,46,94". cor:b2-min l.5515: "Along the tower the counts are 0,4,28,136,600 at k=1,...,5." cor:blowup-transl l.6356: "(P) fails for B^1, B^2 and B^3 themselves (exact arithmetic), so by Cref{cor:blowup-parity} B(B^k,z) fails Holt--Klee for k=1,2,3, every z and every choice of u." I did independently reproduce the route's numbers: from B^2 with z = 4 xor 12 = 8, B^3 has sink 12, height 22 at {44,46,60,62,108,110,124,126}, walk from 44 = 44,83,45,81,40,80,32,71,33,69,36,68,4,27,5,25,0,24,8,15,9,13,12 — exactly as claimed.

findings.defect: Both are existing technique presented as new propositions without naming it. b3:rise-direction is the Green-function step in the proof of thm:impedance (f' - f = N' Delta) with Delta = b_v * Delta(s) instead of Delta supported at one vertex. b3:decompose is elimination of the two outer vertices from the fixed-point system — stochastic complementation, which the paper already attributes to Meyer in def:reduced-rows and lists among the dead ends. The genuinely new observation in b3:decompose is only that val(beta) takes three forms across the four layers, collapsing the design to three substituted systems on one set of rows.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex thm:impedance l.3605, proof: "Both f and f' solve their own systems ... so (I-P')(f'-f)=Delta and f'-f = N' Delta with N' := (I-P')^{-1} = sum_{k>=0}(P')^k, the Green function". def:reduced-rows l.5429: "the first-passage law of the action conditioned on leaving v (Meyer's stochastic complement, from memory)". Neither is cited by the route's proofs.

findings.result_name: b3:residue and the route's headline phrase "the residual obstruction is localised to six explicit inner strategies"
findings.defect: This is the residue of a failed floating-point sequential-LP search, and the project's own record says such failures are not evidence. Calling it "the residual obstruction" over-reads it; the body correctly says "No obstruction is proved", so the headline and the body disagree.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex rem:blowup-measured: "(Blind searches for it, with two or three Min vertices, had not converged, and had also failed to re-find the known walks of G# and of a one-player height-6 game within the same budget; the realisation was found by design, not by search.)" The standing round rules list "blind searches for realisations at m >= 5 (huntG, huntW2, ascendB, realiseAP, bilinear alternation, successive LP -- all failed for hours on a target later realised by design)" as DEAD. The residue set itself I confirmed exactly: {g^{B^2}_{alpha_2} = +} = {17,19,23,25,27,31}, matching the route's six.

findings.result_name: b3:tb — verification (independent re-check) and one free strengthening the route missed
findings.defect: No defect: the game is real, dyadic, built, and verifies from the game. Reported here because it is the route's only durable artefact, and because k = 1 is provably optimal, which the route does not say.
findings.evidence: Independent verifier /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/d1fe2115-9b72-4784-bb94-87421ac1106c/scratchpad/audit-b3/ver.py, exact Fractions, no route code reused: 192 non-sink + 2 sinks = 194; 7 Max, 1 Min, 184 avg; out-degree two everywhere; greatest trap on V minus {t0,t1} is EMPTY, so stopping (lem:trapchar); all 128 val_sigma taken as the componentwise minimum over both Min strategies and the minimum verified attained; 0 tied incidences; outmap equals B_{ptilde,0}(B^2) recomputed independently from B^2 and ptilde; USO and acyclic; sink 4; BA height 12 at {44,46,60,62,108,110,124,126}; run from 44 = 44,83,45,81,40,80,32,71,33,69,36,68,4; val_sigma nondecreasing at all 192 non-sink vertices along the run. Also verified: ptilde differs from h_{B^2} mod 2 at exactly {6,10,20,21,22,26}, none on the walk 12,19,13,17,8,16,0,7,1,5,4, and B_{ptilde,8}(B^2) has height 22 with the same 23-vertex walk as B^3. FREE STRENGTHENING: layer (0,0) of B_{ptilde,0}(B^2) carries B^2 as an inner facet, B^2 is not Holt-Klee, and Holt-Klee is inherited by faces; so by prop:oneplayer-lp no nondegenerate one-player game realises it and by thm:min-count k >= 1 — the single Min vertex is optimal, not merely sufficient.

findings.defect: No defect. This is the route's one genuinely new, load-bearing idea and it should be credited as such: cor:parity-unreadable makes the true parity look unusable, and the route's observation is that b3:free-parity(b) licenses replacing it by any p agreeing along the walk, and that such a p IS affinely readable from the level-two values. That is what makes b3:tb exist at all. Clause (a) is correctly labelled measured (float LP, no Farkas certificate) — it should not be integrated as a proposition clause, and a Farkas certificate here is a small exact LP that could have been produced.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex cor:parity-unreadable l.5547 and the paragraph after it: "This is why the outer pair of a level-two realisation cannot read the inner parity through a Max row difference, which is exactly an affine functional of the value vector." The route's exact witness is the alpha_3/beta_3 rows of TB_nf_D10.json, and my independent check that the resulting outmap is B_{ptilde,0}(B^2) certifies the sign pattern in exact arithmetic.

verdict:
MEANS SOMETHING, BUT MUCH LESS THAN ADVERTISED — integrate about a third of it, reject the headline.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW. Three things. (1) b3:parity-readable: the true parity of h_{B^2} is (measured) not affinely readable from the level-two values, but a p agreeing with it only along the walk is — this is the route's real idea and it is what makes everything else possible. (2) b3:free-parity clause (b) only: the height h(u)+2+h(o xor z), decoupling the walk's start from the translation, and the observation that p is free off the walk. (3) b3:tb: a genuine, dyadic, built, verified game — I re-verified it from the game with my own code (194 vertices, 7 Max, 1 Min, greatest trap empty, no tied incidence, outmap = B_{ptilde,0}(B^2), USO, acyclic, height 12, values nondecreasing along the run). It is the project's first 7-cube realisation and, as I note above, its single Min vertex is provably optimal. Everything else is either already in frontier.tex, already in the Lean file, or a necessary condition on a design shape the route itself chose.

WHAT IS NOT NEW. The headline — "thm:blowup is relaxed (the parity is needed only along the walk, and z is free)" — is two-thirds a restatement of the repository's own machine-checked result. lem:blowup-faces (l.6311) already says B(s,z) is an AUSO for every z, with the identical proof-reading argument; rem:blowup-measured (l.5371) already says the Lean file proves isUSO_blow and isAcyclic_blow "for every z and every parity function"; lean/SSGProof/Blowup.lean l.103/207/313 defines and proves exactly that. Presenting 2600 random samples as the verification of a theorem the project has proved in Lean, without citing it, is the single worst defect here. b3:translate duplicates rem:blowup-measured and cor:blowup-transl's proof; b3:rise-sign is prop:rows-turn/cor:b2-rows applied to the translated coordinate; b3:rise-direction is thm:impedance's Green-function step; b3:decompose is stochastic complementation (Meyer, already cited in def:reduced-rows); B^3's height 22 is in rem:blowup-measured, its 28 forbidden pairs are in cor:b2-min, and its non-Holt-Kleeness is in cor:blowup-transl. None of these is attributed.

CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? No oracle, no target-equivalence problem, and the route claims no barrier — correctly, because b3:rise-sign, b3:two-cycle, b3:theta-floor, b3:decompose and b3:rise-direction cover NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6, def:bsi, R_BR or all-switches. They are necessary conditions on one design shape. b3:two-cycle is close to vacuous relative to the open question: its hypothesis ("the inner vertices do not read the outer pair") is exactly the one-way coupling that cannot produce a translation. b3:theta-floor's punchline is conditional on reusing the published rows. No polynomial class, no lower-bound family, is claimed.

THE CENTRAL SIGNIFICANCE JUDGMENT. b3:tb realises the two ingredients rem:blowup-realise already lists as AVAILABLE — the outer pair alternating every round, and the walk run twice — and does not touch the third, which that same remark names as the obstacle (showing the inner game the anti-value of the translated coordinate). It does so by setting z = 0 and reusing the level-two normal form literally unchanged (I checked all twelve rows), so the coupling is one-way and the inner values are identical in all four layers. Its height 12 is exactly h*(5) + h*(2), lem:hstar-super's additive bound — the linear regime rem:blowup-realise already classifies as settling nothing. So the honest headline is: "the outer table of the blow-up is realisable at +2 Max, +0 Min, +1 bit against an UNTRANSLATED inner game; the translation is untouched." The b3:cost claim that the outer half is additive does not follow, because the outer readout reads the layer-(0,0) inner values that a real translation changes; the two halves are not independent, and the vertex-count column is not a well-defined cost (the paper realises B^1 on 39 vertices, not the 58 the table uses).

TWO THINGS THAT ARE WRONG, NOT MERELY UNORIGINAL. (i) b3:rise-sign(c)'s proof asserts that a coordinate of a USO of dimension >= 2 cannot be constant; the uniform USO of the d-cube refutes that. The lemma needs "g_j non-constant in s", which holds in the intended application. (ii) The route's gap says its row-family statement and the SSG statement are "equivalently" the same; b3:decompose is a sufficient reduction only, so the implication runs one way.

THE TRUE REMAINING GAP, one sentence, stated more precisely than the route: no nondegenerate stopping SSG is known whose improvement outmap is B_{p,z}(B^2) for ANY z /= 0 and ANY p agreeing with h_{B^2} mod 2 along a maximal-height bottom-antipodal walk — with any number of Min vertices, any denominator, and with no assumption that the outer pair carries two-cycle rows or that the inner vertices avoid reading alpha; nothing in this route constrains realisations outside b3:decompose's shape, and nothing in it addresses the anti-value obstacle of rem:blowup-realise.

BETTER OR WORSE? Worse as delivered; better if cut to about a third.
INTEGRATE: b3:tb, as a proposition with the game, the independent verification, and the honest framing (outer table realised, height h+2 = h*(5)+h*(2), z = 0, inner rows unchanged), plus the free strengthening that k = 1 is optimal there. b3:parity-readable, as a remark, with (a) labelled as the float measurement it is. b3:free-parity, as a COROLLARY of lem:blowup-faces and walk_blow carrying only clause (b). b3:theta-floor's first paragraph (the two-cycle pins Theta absolutely) as a short remark with the exact numbers 2048/3313, 2036/3313, 0.5538 — all of which I reproduced exactly. b3:min-role, which is an exact measurement and the most informative single fact in the report about what the level-two Min vertex is for. b3:decompose as a remark inside sec:readouts, attributed to elimination, with "sufficient, not equivalent" said out loud.
DO NOT INTEGRATE: b3:free-parity(a) as a theorem; b3:translate as a lemma; b3:rise-sign as stated; b3:two-cycle as a lemma (keep only its dominance inequality as a design note); b3:b3's forbidden-pair count; b3:residue beyond one sentence; b3:cost's additivity claim and its vertex column.
Finally, on redirection value: this route is on the negative side of the project and closes nothing there. Its one durable contribution to the search is the p-relaxation, which tells the next attempt that the outer readout need not be a parity — and its own failure tells that attempt that the outer half designed against an untranslated inner game is not the half that matters.
